title: Amber Enterprises Bets Big on Smartphone Manufacturing With Oppo, OnePlus, Realme Deal
excerpt: India's leading AC contract manufacturer enters the fiercely competitive mobile assembly segment, targeting 8 million units in year one.
body:
• Amber Enterprises has signed a manufacturing deal with Oppo India to assemble phones for Oppo, OnePlus, and Realme brands starting Q1 FY28.
  • The company targets 8 million units in year one, scaling to 13–15 million by year two, under an asset-light model with capex below ₹50 crore.
  • EBITDA margins in mobile assembly are expected at 1.5–2%, well below Amber's core air-conditioner business but offset by high asset turnover.
  • The three brands collectively shipped 39 million smartphones in India in FY26, though their combined market share has slipped from 28.5% in FY24 to 25.7%.

Amber Enterprises India, the country's largest room air-conditioner contract manufacturer, has entered the smartphone assembly business through a manufacturing collaboration with Oppo Mobiles India — a move that marks its most significant diversification in over two decades.

Under the agreement, executed on June 18, Amber Group will manufacture mobile phones for three brands — Oppo, OnePlus, and Realme — at an existing facility under a sublease arrangement with Oppo India, according to a company disclosure. Trial production is set for Q4 FY27, with commercial operations beginning in Q1 FY28.

Scale and Structure

Management has outlined a production target of approximately 8 million units in the first year of commercial operations, with a calibrated ramp-up to 13–15 million units in the second year, according to an investor conference call covered by NDTV Profit and Communications Today.

https://x.com/EconomicTimes/status/2088957185669865924

"This collaboration highlights the company's manufacturing capabilities and its ability to support globally recognised brands with quality, reliability, value addition and scale."

— Jasbir Singh, Executive Chairman and CEO, Amber Enterprises

The model is designed to be asset-light. Capital expenditure for initial assembly and surface-mount technology (SMT) operations is expected to remain below ₹50 crore, with minimal working capital requirements. The sublease structure also means the arrangement does not require Press Note 3 approval — the mandatory regulatory clearance for foreign direct investment from countries sharing a land border with India.

Thin Margins, High Volumes

Smartphone assembly operates on wafer-thin margins compared with Amber's core air-conditioner business. Management expects EBITDA margins in the range of 1.5–2% excluding Production Linked Incentive (PLI) benefits, according to the concall. JM Financial estimates profit-after-tax margins of around 1%, while Elara Capital pegs them at 1.5%.

For context, market leader Dixon Technologies earns an EBITDA margin of roughly 3% in mobile assembly excluding PLI incentives. Dixon also operates under a stickier original design manufacturer (ODM) arrangement with Oppo through its joint venture Longcheer, according to JM Financial, which noted it does not foresee immediate risks to incumbents.

ICICI Direct took a more positive view, noting that while margins remain sub-3%, the segment benefits from significantly higher asset turns of 8–10x, supporting better return ratios. The brokerage called the development positive for Amber, saying it opens a large new growth avenue and creates potential synergies with ongoing PCB and component localisation efforts.

A Shrinking Customer Base

Amber enters a customer ecosystem that is no longer on an uptrend. Oppo, OnePlus, and Realme together sold approximately 39 million smartphones in India in FY26, accounting for 25.7% market share — a steady decline from 41.4 million units and 28.5% in FY24, according to analysis by Livemint.

Premiumisation has hit Realme hardest, with annual shipments falling from 18.2 million units in FY24 to 14.4 million in FY26. OnePlus, amid organisational restructuring and stiffer competition from Samsung and Vivo, sold just 3.4 million units in FY26 — barely a third of FY24 volumes.

Oppo's existing contracts with other EMS players will continue alongside Amber's arrangement, according to management, suggesting this is an additive manufacturing partnership rather than a consolidation of Oppo's supply chain.

The Bigger Picture for Amber

Amber has spent more than two decades building its position from a pure-play AC contract manufacturer into one of India's largest electronics manufacturing services companies. The company has diversified into consumer electronics, wearables, printed circuit boards, railway electronics, and components, aided by acquisitions including Power-One, Unitronics, and Shogini.

For FY26, the company reported consolidated revenue of ₹7,967 crore and net profit of ₹146 crore, according to exchange filings. The electronics division was a standout performer, with revenues growing 49% year-over-year and operating EBITDA climbing 89%, per Bajaj Broking analysis. Management has projected the electronics division to maintain roughly 40% revenue growth in FY27.

The smartphone bet fits Amber's broader strategy of balancing high-value-added operations with volume manufacturing, though analysts remain divided. HDFC Securities downgraded the stock to REDUCE in May 2026 with a target of ₹7,580, citing weak Q4 FY26 performance and near-term cost inflation from rising commodity prices.

What to Watch

The key questions for investors revolve around execution and margin trajectory. Amber must build supply-chain efficiencies from scratch in a segment where incumbents like Dixon already have years of operating leverage. Component localisation — particularly in PCBs — will be critical to improving margins beyond the initial 1.5–2% range.

For the broader Make in India story, the deal underscores the continued shift of smartphone manufacturing into domestic facilities. India is now the world's second-largest smartphone market, and the government's PLI scheme has been a significant pull factor for EMS expansion, even as the second phase of PLI incentives remains under development.
